about: Health Monitor's event-log checks on Windows: disk and file-system problems logged in the last event_days days, and events counted since the last restart. Each check names its log, its event ID and the providers that write it; an ID other providers also use (129 is also the Time Service's) is matched only with its providers. A check with events found is a finding at its severity.

checks.meaning: The disk has a bad block.
The disk driver detected a controller error.
The disk was not ready for access.
An error was detected on the disk during a paging operation.
The disk reports that it is predicted to fail.
An I/O operation on the disk was retried.
The disk was removed while in use.
The storage driver reset the device after a request did not complete in time.
NTFS found corruption in the file system structure.
NTFS could not flush data to the transaction log.
ReFS found a checksum error it could not correct.
Chkdsk ran on a volume at startup; the event holds its result.
A desktop heap allocation failed: programs in that session can fail to start or to open windows.
